lead_headline: Foreclosures surge 37% week-over-week to 48 filings while restaurant tracker adds 6 leads—Ash and Agave debuts Cherry Creek coastal Mexican today, Hip Hop Ice Cream opens Sloan Lake storefront

restaurant.blurb: 6 new leads today (3 openings, 3 closures) hold active inventory steady at 88 cases (45 openings, 43 closures)—Saturday's batch includes Ash and Agave opening today at Cherry Creek Shopping Center (coastal Mexican from Shucking Good Hospitality, confidence 10), Hip Hop Ice Cream Shop launching Sloan Lake storefront at former McMahan Cleaners site (confidence 8), recategorized Colfax and Cream Washington Park West entry. Closures: Dairy Queen at 2897 W Belleview Fort Logan confirmed shuttered (confidence 8, third DQ closure this week completes Westminster-Littleton-Fort Logan trifecta), two legacy reclassifications. Week's close: 23 opening leads vs 6 closure leads across 7 days, with Union Station corridor (Ogo Sushi, Mendocino Farms, G-Que BBQ, C Burger) dominating new-concept geography while chain casualties (DQ trilogy, CPK, Einstein Bros) drive closure inventory.

foreclosure.blurb: 48 filings this week jump 37% from prior week's 35, with top case capping at $1.1M Douglas County (14247 Beebalm Loop)—no $2M+ properties as 93 auctions queue next 7 days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today—April 5 extends statewide filing freeze to 36 consecutive days, now 200% beyond December 2024's 12-day record and blowing past all database precedent. Six straight zero-filing days (March 31-April 5) confirm systemic halt, not processing lag—no social chatter, no regulatory announcements, suggesting 75-95 application backlog awaiting system restoration. Database shows 12,326 historical cases with zero precedent for 5+ week void outside declared emergencies. Monday's reading critical: seventh consecutive zero triggers mandatory escalation to Liquor Enforcement Division as alternative hypothesis (legislative freeze, regulatory moratorium) finds no supporting evidence in statehouse tracking or agency communications.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday close week at 58 citations (+2% vs prior week's 57) across 17 sources—Saturday's mix includes Denver Post development coverage, Instagram Larimer Square retail reshares, Facebook Continental redevelopment threads. Instagram holds weekly crown (14 mentions) narrowly edging Denver Post (13) and Facebook (11), maintaining social platform dominance at 48% weekly share (Instagram/Facebook/X combined 27 of 58). Week-over-week source diversity ticks up (17 vs 16 prior), but mention volume flatlines—rolling 30-day average steadies at 54 mentions/week as April's first five days track 3.6/day vs March's 3.2 opening pace, suggesting seasonal uptick solidifying though still shy of February's 4.1/day peak.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +0 yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) marks second consecutive flat Saturday—MTD holds at −1 (−0.2/day) as 90-day net sustains +136. Five-day April start: +3 net (13 new, 10 canceled, 0.6 net/day) vs March's opening quintet (+17 net, 3.4/day), confirming 82% acquisition deceleration. Past 7 days post +4 net (18 new, 14 canceled, 56% retention) vs prior week's +22 (29 new, 7 canceled, 81% retention)—churn spike persists as weekend zero-activity pattern suggests structural weekend conversion gap. Longer view: YTD +130 (+1.4/day) cushions MTD stumble, but April needs +31 net by month-end to match Q1 pace—current 0.6/day trajectory delivers +15 if sustained, creating 16-subscriber Q1-to-Q2 gap and signaling potential seasonal headwinds or product-market friction requiring diagnosis.
